verdicts.title: One contact verdict: the kernel decides guard/perfect, the ledger reads it
verdicts.premise_notes: kernel.ts:98-110 checked: the contact tap fires at :99 before any gate, Air evade returns at :101, the ward is :106, the exchangeGuard window is :109, perfect with !suppressPerfect is :110. ledger.ts:58-63 re-derives wardUp/inArc/age/window from raw state; gradeContact :37 guarded = wardUp && inArc; observeLedger :94 downgrades a guarded mismatch to unclassified. exchange.ts:55 is exchangeGuard. answers.ts:10/:23 print 'Unclassified N'. I reproduced the evidence with a scratchpad tsx probe at HEAD (reference vs fire_close, seeds 1-4, ledger on the player): 202/272 unclassified, and 0/42 under exchangeOff. Both match the card exactly. The ledger is consumed by named-census, report-w4, runFight, bout-reader, counter-coverage and arena-entry. New Answer kinds flow through emptyAnswerCounts; seed:hash digests do not read answer counts, so no evidence digest moves. The only Answer enumerations outside ledger.ts are answers.ts and combat-readout.test.ts. This card should land before arena-render B, which plans to predict from gradeContact.
verdicts.ambition_why: It removes a duplicated rule seam that misreports 74% of close-fight contacts to the player. That is a real architectural fix with a visible payoff, not a tidy-up.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every anchor holds and the headline number reproduces exactly (202/272, 0/42 under exchangeOff).
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Case 1 is a measured red today. Case 6 is an agreement property against the kernel's own events. Case 7 forbids edits to the goldens and parity files. A wrong build fails a test, and every case can be written red first.
extra_files_needed: packages/core/src/arena/index.ts (export contact.ts if arena-render B or the game reads contactVerdict)

verdicts.title: Compile enemy behaviour once: a typed table replaces 17 id branches and prose regex
verdicts.premise_notes: The grep count of spec.id/attack.id compares in enemies.ts is 17, as claimed (the file is 107 lines). extract() throws 'Missing enemy magnitude' at :17. backoffS re-parses at :20 and is called from :37 and :54. The per-tick regex at :66, :76 and :81 is confirmed. Golden coverage of the roster is thin, so the case 1 characterization series is genuinely needed. As written, case 3 greps enemies.ts only, so a build could move the 17 id compares verbatim into enemy-behaviour.ts and pass.
verdicts.ambition_why: Turning 17 branches in a 107-line file into a table is a worthwhile cleanup, but it is closer to a tidy-up than a principal's move; impact 7 is generous.
verdicts.grounding_why: The counts, line anchors and the mid-bout throw path are all verified in the tree.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Case 1 hash-series parity is strong. But case 3 can be satisfied by relocating the id branches rather than replacing them with data.
verdicts.revision: Extend case 3: also grep packages/core/src/arena/enemy-behaviour.ts. Each roster id may appear there at most once, and only as a key of the single compiled behaviour table. No `spec.id ===`/`attack.id ===` comparison may appear in either file.

The campActions ladder is at :389-416, with the PLOT label special-cased at :422. The SCHEME_eve cap appears at camp-session.ts:181-184 and camp.ts:340-344, with remainingCaps stripping _eve at :149. verdicts.title: Contest odds on every camp action and parley card, from the resolver's own DC
verdicts.premise_notes: The contest formulas are confirmed: WATCH at camp.ts:595-598, REPORT :615-617, SCHEME :643-662 (patrol term, persuade/rumour DCs, b.warned at :655, stopped-set, rumourFailsAtOrBelow at :660), CAUGHT :719-721 and RECRUIT :748-752. parley.ts:210-213 rolls against contestDc 15 (parley.json:8), and parleyCards :104-114 returns no odds. rules.json contests show d20, multiplier 4, baseDc 10, vigilBonus 8. The screens/camp.ts:135 subtitle is as quoted. The 0.06 empirical tolerance at 400 seeds is too loose: a '>' vs '>=' off-by-one shifts odds by exactly 0.05 and would pass cases 2, 3 and 5. Case 1 catches it only for the bare helper, not for the per-contest bonus/dc builders. Showing odds also lets the player infer NPC guile; that design call is correctly gated as direction.
verdicts.ambition_why: It turns every blind camp contest into an informed bet, from the resolver's own math. That is a meaningful decision-quality elevation.
verdicts.grounding_why: All formula sites and data values verified.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: The agreement tests cannot tell a die off-by-one (0.05) inside a 0.06 tolerance.
verdicts.revision: In cases 2, 3 and 5, add an exact check alongside the 400-seed empirical one: for each contest, the bonus/dc the preview's builder returns must equal the bonus/dc the resolver records in its Roll (rolls.at(-1).score - die value, rolls.at(-1).dc) on the same planted state, so the preview and resolver share inputs exactly and the 0.06 tolerance only guards the closed form.
extra_files_needed: packages/core/src/parley.test.ts (if parley odds are asserted there)

verdicts.title: One census kernel: a fight runner with read-only observers and one report harness
verdicts.premise_notes: The loop sites are confirmed at builds-census.ts:34, counter-coverage.ts:81, named-census.ts:18, week-census.ts:89/99 and report-ladder.ts:13 (and :25). Outcome mappings, seed:hash digests and median helpers are as listed; builds returns 0 on empty, weeks returns null. The armed runWeekBuildFight at week-census.ts:94-101 returns 5 fields. d1-exchange-after fire_close digest dd746f4e is verified. Case 7 cannot pass as written: report-w4.ts:38/42/46 and report-named.ts:27 also call createHash('sha256'), for digests and for source-file hashes, and report-w4.ts is outside the write set ('stays'). Overlap: progression A's createGames opponentMage option removes the armed fork that case 3 targets. Build progression A first, then case 3 reduces to routing through runBuildFight. Write-set collision on builds-census.ts/report-builds.ts with schools-ai B.
verdicts.ambition_why: A solid consolidation of six loop forks into one observer-based runner, but it is internal tooling; the armed-reading gain is shared with progression A.
verdicts.grounding_why: All anchors hold, but case 7's grep claim ignores report-w4.ts and report-named.ts file-hash uses.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Fixture parity plus committed digests catch any moved fight. Case 7 would fail even on a correct build.
verdicts.revision: Narrow case 7's grep to the seed:hash digest expression (`${f.seed}:${f.hash}` fed to createHash) in the files this card ports. report-w4.ts and the source-file hashOf at report-named.ts:27 stay out of scope.

verdicts.title: census:compare - two evidence files in, the D1 before/after table out, with noise verdicts
verdicts.premise_notes: I probed the committed files. d1-exchange-before/after summaries have the claimed values (fire_close 0.47/15.82/04b7e871 -> 0.495/66.95/dd746f4e; air_close 0.525 -> 0.40), both with seedRange [40000,40199]. d1-weeks vs d1-weeks-arm-lag week-1 digests are 20 equal and 0 differ. W8 named.json wave 3 is 0.5515/16.45 and d1-named-after wave 3 is 0.4455/62.95. Wilson(0.40, 200) = [0.335, 0.469] and z = 2.51 are confirmed. The scripts have no compare script. One defect: case 7 expects '16.5 -> 63.0', but (16.45).toFixed(1) is '16.4' in JS (binary rounding), so the case either fails or forces an unstated rounding rule. This is a purely additive reader with no simulator effect.
verdicts.ambition_why: It turns hand-transcribed D1 tables and eyeballed noise into a computed verdict. That is a real gain for operator workflow, at modest scope.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every number in the cases matches the committed evidence.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: The cases are exact values over committed files and are red today. The only issue is one rounding expectation.
verdicts.revision: In case 7, replace 'Brennic median 16.5 -> 63.0 s' with '16.4 -> 63.0 s (durationS.p50 16.45 -> 62.95 rendered with toFixed(1))', or state an explicit round-half-up rule in the renderer and assert it in case 6.
